metaTitle: DiDi Pay in China (2026): Foreign Card, Alipay or WeChat Pay
metaDescription: Three ways to pay for DiDi in China with a foreign card: the DiDi app, Alipay or WeChat Pay. Plus the ¥200 fee rule and what to do if your card fails.
heading: DiDi Pay for Foreigners: How to Pay for DiDi in China

byline.name: Maintained by Lin
byline.tested: Rules checked against DiDi's official app listing and Chinese government payment guides, October 24, 2026

quickAnswer: Yes, you can pay for DiDi with a foreign card. There are three ways:

items: **In the DiDi China app.** Add your card in the app. DiDi's official listing says the app works in English, accepts foreign phone numbers and takes international bank cards.
**Through Alipay.** Open the DiDi mini program inside Alipay. The fare is charged to the card you linked in Alipay.
**Through WeChat.** The same, paid with WeChat Pay.

quickAnswer: If you pay through Alipay or WeChat Pay with a foreign card, rides of ¥200 or less are generally fee-free. Above ¥200, a 3% fee may apply to the whole fare. And don't plan on cash: DiDi rides are paid in the app.
Jump to: [Which to choose](#compare) · [DiDi app](#card) · [Alipay or WeChat](#alipay-wechat) · [Fees](#fees) · [Declined card](#declined) · [Wrong or double charge](#charges)

cta.text: **Flying soon?** I'll get DiDi, Alipay and WeChat Pay working on your phone before you fly, so your first ride from the airport isn't a payment puzzle.

blocks.text: All three work with a foreign bank card. They differ in what you set up and what you may pay in fees.

The app, plus a phone number that can receive an SMS code (foreign numbers work)

WeChat Pay with your card linked

Cards with UnionPay, Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Diners Club or Discover logos may be accepted
Same as Alipay

Paying with your card: no wallet fee. Your bank may charge a foreign transaction fee

blocks.text: **My advice: set up two.** Add your card in the DiDi app, and link a card in Alipay as well. If DiDi declines your card, open DiDi inside Alipay and you're still on your way.

sections.title: Pay in the DiDi China app with your card

items: Install **DiDi China: Ride Hailing**, the app for mainland China. Sign in with your phone number (you'll need to receive one SMS code) and switch the app to English. Full setup: [how to use DiDi in China](/didi-in-china-for-foreigners/).
Add your international bank card in the app's payment settings. Your bank may ask you to confirm with a code or in its app.
When you book, check the payment method on the booking screen before you confirm. If it shows Alipay or WeChat Pay instead of your card, the wallet fee rule below applies.
The fare is charged when the ride ends. Open the trip afterwards to check it's marked as paid.

blocks.text: Before you fly, turn on overseas and online payments in your banking app, or tell your bank you'll be in China, so your first DiDi charge isn't blocked as suspicious.

sections.title: Pay through Alipay or WeChat instead

blocks.text: If your card is already linked in Alipay or WeChat Pay, you don't need the DiDi app.

items: **Alipay:** search for 滴滴出行 (DiDi's Chinese name) in Alipay and open the DiDi mini program. Book as usual. The fare is paid from Alipay, which charges your linked card.
**WeChat:** search for 滴滴出行 in WeChat and open the DiDi mini program. The fare is paid with WeChat Pay.

blocks.text: Haven't linked a card yet? Do it before you fly: [Alipay for foreigners](/alipay-for-foreigners/) · [WeChat Pay for foreigners](/wechat-pay-for-foreigners/).
When a ride is paid through Alipay or WeChat Pay with a foreign card:

items: **¥200 or less:** generally no platform fee.
**Over ¥200:** a 3% fee may apply to the whole amount. On a ¥250 airport ride, that's ¥7.50.

blocks.text: Most rides within a city cost less than ¥200, but long airport transfers can cost more. For those, pay with your card in the DiDi app: the wallet fee doesn't apply, though your bank's foreign transaction fee still can.
The price you see before booking can change with the route, tolls or waiting time. What you actually paid is in the trip record.

sections.title: If your card is declined or a payment fails

rows: The card won't add
Look for a blocked attempt in your banking app and approve it, or call your bank. Or try a different card, in DiDi or in Alipay.
Payment failed after the ride
Open the trip and pay the fare with another method before your next ride.
Your bank shows a charge, but DiDi says unpaid
Don't pay again straight away. It may be a pending authorization. Check again later, and contact DiDi support if you end up charged twice.

blocks.text: Don't hand the driver cash to fix a failed payment: the app can still show the trip as unpaid. Settle it in the app.

items: Open the trip in DiDi and compare the fare with what your bank shows.
Two amounts for one ride in your bank app? One is often a pending authorization that drops off on its own. Give it a few days.
If DiDi itself shows two payments, or the fare looks wrong, contact DiDi's in-app customer service. DiDi says English support is available 24/7.

blocks.text: Take screenshots of the trip and your bank's entry before you contact support.

faqs.question: Can I pay for DiDi with a foreign credit card?
faqs.answer: Yes. DiDi's official listing says the DiDi China app accepts international bank cards. You can also link your card in Alipay or WeChat Pay and book through the DiDi mini program there.

faqs.question: Which cards does DiDi accept?
faqs.answer: DiDi's listing doesn't name the card networks for its app. Through Alipay or WeChat Pay, cards with UnionPay, Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Diners Club or Discover logos may be accepted.

faqs.question: Do I need Alipay or WeChat Pay to use DiDi?
faqs.answer: No. The DiDi China app works on its own with a foreign phone number and a foreign bank card. Alipay is a good backup if your card is declined.

faqs.question: Is there a fee for paying DiDi with a foreign card?
faqs.answer: Through Alipay or WeChat Pay, rides of ¥200 or less are generally fee-free; above ¥200, a 3% fee may apply to the whole fare. Your bank may also charge its own foreign transaction fee.

faqs.question: Can I pay the DiDi driver in cash?
faqs.answer: Plan on paying in the app. Beijing's government guide for new arrivals says DiDi "is not a cash-friendly transportation system". If you want to pay cash, take a street taxi.

faqs.question: What if DiDi charged me twice?
faqs.answer: Check the trip in DiDi first. A second amount in your bank app is often a pending authorization that drops off. If DiDi itself shows two payments, contact its in-app English support.
